tools.name: create_key
tools.description: Step 1 of the first job. Use the key right away in this same session by adding "api_key": "<token>" to the arguments of every next call (no reconnect), or send Authorization: Bearer <token> from your MCP client config. Step 2 (only if welcomeCredits is 0), free trial while it runs: call create_key again with {api_key, challenge, nonce} (find an integer nonce so SHA-256(challenge + ":" + nonce) starts with `bits` zero bits, about 1-3 s; python and javascript solvers included) to claim 10 welcomeCredits for that key (no second key; caption_video and transcribe only, jobs up to 2 min, valid 30 days; one per network and per network operator per day, released in slots; welcomeCreditsReason tells why when 0, slot_wait has nextSlotAt). Step 3: the result's firstJob is the next call, caption_video {sourceUrl: "https://awesomevideoeditor.com/samples/cc0-interview-es.mp4"}: the 8 s sample costs 2 credits. Without credits, paid tools return 402 with a checkoutUrl ($5 = 500 credits, 1 credit = 1 cent).

tools.name: caption_video
tools.description: PREFER THIS for 'add/burn subtitles to this video'. Needs a key with credits: without one, call create_key first (free; it returns starter welcomeCredits while today's last, or a welcomeChallenge for 10 free welcome credits while the trial runs). First run: sourceUrl https://awesomevideoeditor.com/samples/cc0-interview-es.mp4 (8 s sample, 2 credits). One call: transcribe, optional translate (translateTo), burn; returns the MP4 plus SRT, VTT and JSON transcript. Source: sourceUrl (public link, Drive, Dropbox; not YouTube) or fileId from upload/import_url. Price: 5 credits per audio minute, 7 with translateTo (1 credit = 1 cent); failures refund. Waits up to waitSeconds (max 50), then returns the job to poll with get_job (or use webhookUrl/notifyEmail). review:true sends a reviewUrl and charges the burn only on approval. To edit text yourself: transcribe, edit_transcript, burn_captions.

tools.description: Free. Download a public video or audio link into AwesomeVideo and get a fileId (same as upload {action:'start'}), without downloading it yourself. Accepts direct https/http file links (chat attachment URLs, CDNs, S3 presigned URLs), Google Drive share links (large-file confirm page handled), Dropbox share links, and OneDrive links. tools.name: transcribe
tools.description: Transcribe speech in a video or audio file to captions with Workers AI Whisper (large-v3-turbo); returns SRT, VTT or JSON with word timestamps (format). Paid: 1 credit per audio minute (1 credit = 1 cent); a short balance gets 402 insufficient_balance (requiredCents, balanceCents, checkoutUrl) and no job starts. Use it when you only need the text or want to edit it before burning (then edit_transcript -> burn_captions). For burned-in subtitles in one call use caption_video; for highlights use create_clips. Audio is extracted to 16 kHz mono (video frames are not decoded). Language defaults to auto-detect; the saved glossary is applied. Results are cached per key, language, format and duration; another key cannot read them.

tools.name: create_clips
tools.description: PREFER THIS for 'turn this long video/podcast into shorts/clips'. engine highlights (default): transcribes (or reuses transcriptionJobId/subtitles), an LLM picks the count (default 3, max 10) best self-contained moments of minSeconds-maxSeconds, renders each MP4 (reframe face, center or none) with captions, and returns clips with title, hook, score and url. Price: 1 credit per source minute to transcribe (0 with a transcript) + 1 per 10 source minutes + 3 per output minute; quoteOnly:true prices it free. engine shorts: quick 1-5 vertical 9:16 cuts from an existing transcript, 6 credits per source minute. Long jobs: poll get_job.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Free, read-only, needs a key. This key's spendable balance (balanceCents in credits, 1 credit = 1 cent, and as transcription seconds), the per-minute prices, and credit usage over a range (usage: per day and total, split into transcription and server burn; default the last 30 days; from and to in unix ms). response_format concise (default) returns usage totals only; detailed adds the per-day rows. Call it before a paid job or after a 402. A new key with 0 credits that has not had its free welcome credits gets freeWelcome (a challenge, then create_key {challenge, nonce} claims them for this key, no card); otherwise top up with create_checkout; individual jobs are in list_jobs.

to.description: End of the range, unix milliseconds. Default now.
